questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct pair of prepositions:
"The qualified technical candidate applied ___ the Registrar General ___ the post of System Assistant."
questions.explanation: Jis authority ya officer ko aavedan bheja jaye uske pehle 'Apply TO' lagta hai ('applied to the Registrar General'); aur jis vacancy ya post ke liye apply kiya jaye uske pehle 'Apply FOR' lagta hai ('applied for the post').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Confusing Relational Pairs — Apply TO (Authority) vs Apply FOR (Post).
questions.hint: Pehle blank mein recipient authority hai, doosre mein desired job position.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Direct Transitive Verbs: Zero Preposition with 'Order'
questions.question: Choose the grammatically accurate sentence:

options.text: The administrative department ordered for twenty high-resolution monitors.
The administrative department ordered twenty high-resolution monitors.
The administrative department ordered about twenty high-resolution monitors to be bought.
The administrative department ordered to twenty high-resolution monitors.

questions.explanation: Verb 'order' jab goods, equipment ya food mangwane ke liye use hoti hai, toh direct transitive hoti hai aur koi preposition nahi leti ('ordered twenty monitors'). Iske sath 'for' lagana classic pleonastic error hai. (Agar 'order' noun hota: 'placed an order for monitors', tab 'for' valid hota).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Order goods (NO for!).
questions.hint: 'Order' jab verb ho toh 'for' lagta hai ya zero preposition?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate grammatical form:
"Being an experienced court clerk, he is accustomed to ___ late into the night during budget sessions."
questions.explanation: 'Be accustomed to' fixed idiomatic phrase mein 'to' Preposition hai, infinitive particle nahi. Preposition ke baad aane wali verb strictly GERUND (-ing form) hoti hai: 'accustomed to working'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — accustomed to + V-ING.
questions.hint: Check karein: 'accustomed to' ke baad V1 lagta hai ya -ing form?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The Special Anti-Corruption Court acquitted the senior accounts officer ___ all allegations of bribery."
questions.explanation: 'Acquit' kisi person ko apradh ya aarop se bari karne ke liye strictly preposition 'OF' leta hai: 'acquitted the officer OF all allegations'. Hindi bolchal se prabhavit hokar '*acquitted from' chunna common mistake hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Acquit OF the offence.
questions.hint: Hindi mein 'aarop se bari' bolte hain, lekin English mein 'of' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Spot the error in the following sentence:
"The Chief Justice / emphasized on the necessity / of judicial digital literacy. / No error"
questions.explanation: Verb 'emphasize' direct transitive verb hai aur bina kisi preposition ke seedhe direct object leti hai ('emphasized the necessity'). Iske sath 'on' lagana galat hai. (Dhyan dein: Noun form mein 'put emphasis ON' valid hota hai, par verb form mein strictly zero preposition!).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Emphasize (NO on!).
questions.hint: 'Emphasize' verb ke turant baad 'on' aana chahiye ya nahi?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Causal Vectors: Result FROM vs Result IN
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"The sudden slowdown of the court management portal resulted ___ a severe cyber DDoS attack on the gateway."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein subject 'The sudden slowdown' Parinaam (Outcome) hai aur object 'a severe cyber DDoS attack' Kaaran (Cause) hai. Jab Outcome subject hota hai, toh formula 'Outcome + resulted FROM + Cause' lagta hai (slowdown attack ki wajah se hua).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Causal & Result Vectors — Outcome resulted FROM Cause.
questions.hint: Check karein: portal slowdown attack ka kaaran hai ya attack ka parinaam?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"Only candidates possessing a recognized diploma in computer applications are eligible ___ this administrative recruitment."
questions.explanation: Kisi pad, exam, scheme ya eligibility ke reference mein adjective 'eligible' hamesha preposition 'FOR' leta hai: 'eligible FOR recruitment'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Adjective + Preposition Core Collocations — Eligible FOR post/exam.
questions.hint: 'Eligible' ke sath 'to' lagta hai ya 'for'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Prepositional 'TO' + Gerund: With A View To
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: The committee was formed with a view to accelerate judicial recruitment.
The committee was formed with a view to accelerating judicial recruitment.
The committee was formed with a view of accelerate judicial recruitment.
The committee was formed with a view at accelerating judicial recruitment.

questions.explanation: 'With a view to' ek fixed idiomatic connective hai jisme 'to' preposition of purpose hai. Preposition ke baad verb strictly GERUND (-ing form) mein aati hai: 'with a view to accelerating'. Bare infinitive (accelerate) lagana incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — With a view to + V-ING.
questions.hint: 'With a view to' ke baad bare verb aati hai ya -ing form?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"Prior ___ the formal inauguration of the server room, an exhaustive security audit was conducted."
questions.explanation: 'Prior' ek Latin comparative adjective hai jo hamesha preposition 'TO' leta hai ('prior TO the event'). Iske sath 'than' ya 'of' lagana severe grammatical error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Comparative Preposition Law — Prior TO (Never Than!).
questions.hint: Latin comparative 'prior' ke sath kaunsa preposition lagta hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Noun Collocations: Cause OF vs Reason FOR
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The forensic team is investigating the exact cause ___ the catastrophic server outage."
questions.explanation: Kisi physical incident, mishap, bimari ya breakdown ka direct source batane ke liye noun 'cause' hamesha preposition 'OF' leta hai ('cause OF the outage'). Action ke explanation ke liye 'reason FOR' lagta hai ('reason FOR the delay').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Noun + Preposition Syntactic Units — Cause OF vs Reason FOR.
questions.hint: Incident ya outage ka direct source batane ke liye 'cause of' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"The judicial inspection team / reached to the district court / before the proceedings began. / No error"
questions.explanation: Verb 'reach' transitively kisi destination par pahunchna denote karti hai aur direct object leti hai ('reached the district court'). Iske sath preposition 'to' lagana pleonastic error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Reach place (NO to!).
questions.hint: 'Reach' ke baad 'to' lagta hai ya direct destination aati hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"Any clerk found attempting to tamper ___ digital judicial records will face immediate suspension."
questions.explanation: Official documents, data ya software ke sath anadhikrit chhedchhad karne ke liye standard legal collocation strictly 'TAMPER WITH' hoti hai ('tamper with records').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Tamper WITH records.
questions.hint: Records ke sath unauthorized chhedchhad ke liye 'tamper with' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:

options.text: The fraudulent stamp resembles with the genuine court seal.
The fraudulent stamp resembles to the genuine court seal.
The fraudulent stamp resembles the genuine court seal.
The fraudulent stamp resembles at the genuine court seal.

questions.explanation: 'Resemble' ek direct transitive verb hai jiska direct object bina kisi preposition ke aata hai ('resembles the court seal'). Iske sath 'with' ya 'to' lagana unnecessary pleonasm hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: The Direct Transitive Law — Resemble (NO to/with!).
questions.hint: 'Resemble' ke baad 'with' ya 'to' lagta hai ya seedhe object aata hai?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate form:
"The standing counsel vehemently objected to the court ___ unverified electronic printouts as evidence."
questions.explanation: 'Object to' phrase mein 'to' Preposition hai. Iske baad aane wala action mandatory GERUND (-ing form) hota hai: 'objected to admitting'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Preposition + Gerund Law — object to + V-ING.
questions.hint: 'Object to' ke baad bare verb aayegi ya -ing form?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Adjective + Preposition: Angry WITH vs Angry AT
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The presiding judge was angry ___ the public prosecutor for submitting an incomplete chargesheet."
questions.explanation: Jab gussa kisi vyakti (human being) par ho, toh formula 'angry WITH a person' lagta hai ('angry with the prosecutor'). Agar gussa kisi aacharan ya sthiti par ho, tab 'angry at/about' lagta hai ('angry at the delay').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Evaluative & Emotional Adjectives — Angry WITH a person vs Angry AT conduct.
questions.hint: Gussa kisi vyakti (prosecutor) par hai ya kisi abstract ghatna par?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"Rigorous typing discipline and conceptual clarity are the key ___ cracking the competitive exam."
questions.explanation: Safalta ya kisi target ki chabi ke context mein noun 'key' hamesha preposition 'TO' demand karta hai: 'key TO success'. 'Key of success' common Indian spoken error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Noun + Preposition Syntactic Units — Key TO success.
questions.hint: Safalta ki chabi ke liye 'key of' hota hai ya 'key to'?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Statutory Collocations: Vested IN vs Vested WITH
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"Under Article 227 of the Constitution, superintendence over all subordinate courts is vested ___ the High Court."
questions.explanation: Jab shaktiyaan kisi constitutional body ya pad ke andar nihit hone ki baat ho, toh formula 'powers are vested IN the authority' lagta hai. (Jab officer ko shaktiyon se endowed kiya jaye tab 'vested with powers' hota hai).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Statutory & Administrative Preposition Concord — Power is vested IN the authority.
questions.hint: Power authority ke andar nihit hai, isliye 'in' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Verb + Preposition: Abstain FROM vs Refrain FROM
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition:
"All government servants are strictly instructed to abstain ___ political campaigning."
questions.explanation: 'Abstain', 'refrain', 'prohibit', aur 'prevent' sabhi hamesha preposition 'FROM' lete hain aur iske baad mandatory Gerund (-ing) aata hai: 'abstain FROM political campaigning'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Verb + Preposition Core Collocations — Abstain/Refrain FROM.
questions.hint: 'Abstain' aur 'refrain' ke sath 'from' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition:
"The revision petition was summarily dismissed as it was completely devoid ___ substantial legal grounds."
questions.explanation: Adjective 'devoid' (se vanchit ya poori tarah khali hona) hamesha preposition 'OF' leta hai: 'devoid OF merit / devoid OF legal grounds'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Adjective + Preposition Core Collocations — Devoid OF merit.
questions.hint: 'Devoid' ke sath hamesha 'of' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Identify the option in which ALL prepositions are used correctly according to standard legal English:

options.text: He preferred arbitration than court, and applied for the Chief Justice with leave.
He discussed about the appeal, entered into the courtroom, and disposed off the case.
He is senior to me, complies with all rules, and disposed of the file expeditiously.
He was accused for bribery, but the bench agreed with the proposal of promotion.

questions.explanation: Option C flawless hai: 'senior TO me' (Latin comparative with 'to'), 'complies WITH' (standard collocation), aur 'disposed OF' (single 'f' disposal). Option A mein 'preferred than' galat hai; Option B mein 'discussed about', 'entered into', aur 'disposed off' teeno errors hain; Option D mein 'accused for' (should be of) aur 'agreed with the proposal' (should be to) galat hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rules RC-07, RC-08, RC-10: Comprehensive Fixed Preposition Architecture.
questions.hint: Check karein: senior to, complies with, aur dispose of (single 'f') kahan ek sath sahi hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L12
